text.p: Following are the main stories in Wednesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- YTL Corp Bhd, the flagship of the Yeoh Tiong Lay family, announced that it had "irrevocably decided not to make any offer for Consolidated Electric Power Asia Ltd (CEPA)" but acknowledged it had successfully lined up funds for the planned takeover including 2.5 billion ringgit from Khazanah National Bhd, the government's investment arm.
- Developers of the KL LinearCity development defended the project as environmentally sound and said it did not violate any environmental regulations.
- Tenaga Nasional Bhd's future is intertwined with that of the economy but the country cannot wait for Tenaga if it does not keep pace, its executive chairman said.

- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad slammed critics who are quick to condemn development projects even before work can start. He was witnessing the signing for the KL LinearCity project, said to be the world's longest building.
